one_month_reasoning: The dominant event falls inside the window and has a confirmed date: Penguin reports fiscal Q4 and FY2026 (year ended 2026-08-28) after the close on Tue 2026-10-06, with a 4:30pm ET call. As of 2026-10-05 it has not been reported, and EDGAR shows no 8-K since July 17 (only routine Oct 1 Form 4 RSU grants). The bar, corrected: 9M FY26 non-GAAP EPS was $1.83 (Q3 release), so the $2.60 +/-0.05 FY guide implies Q4 EPS of about $0.77 (range $0.72-0.82). That equals the street's $0.77 / $519M rather than sitting below it as I said in round 1, so a simple 'beat' carries no edge. The reaction will turn on the first formal FY27 outlook against the $3.34 consensus (raised from $2.81 in 30 days, 7 up / 0 down, already near management's call-only ~30% framing), on Integrated Memory pricing durability (57% of Q3 sales) and on gross margin (28.1% in Q3 vs 31.2% in Q2). The stock jumped about 11.6% on Oct 2 into the print, which raises the bar a little. Against that are upward revisions and SK hynix's purchase of the preferred at about $62.4 per as-converted share, a strategic holder that reduces overhang. I see no directional edge, so the distribution is a near-symmetric lognormal centred at about $61.4 with sigma about 23.5% (83% annual / 3.5, which already embeds a +/-15-20% earnings-day move).

fair_value.method: Blend of 16.5x NTM-at-horizon EPS $3.88 = $64.0 (weight 0.65), today's 16.5x CY27 $3.51 = $57.9 rolled forward at 10% = $63.7 (0.2), and a corrected EV/EBITDA proxy (preferred counted as 6.10M shares, $176M principal net debt) = $63.4 (0.15), for about $64. 16.5x is 13% under the 18.95x CY27 median of 10 peers.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM-at-horizon EPS (Oct-2027 to Sep-2028, about FY28 plus one month) $3.88 x 16.5x = $64.0. This is the price the stock should carry in Oct-2027 if the market keeps paying a peer-relative NTM multiple. 16.5x is about 13% below the 18.95x CY27 median of 10 peers and inside the peer range.

inputs_detail.derivation: 9M = Q1 $0.47 + Q2 $0.52 + Q3 $0.84 = $1.83 per the Q3 release (I mis-added $1.85 in round 1).
Alpha Vantage mean of 7 analysts. stockanalysis's $3.38 is management's ~30% framing, not an independent count.
No FY28 consensus exists from any reachable source. +15% on $3.34, slower than FY27 because the Integrated Memory price lift (+111% y/y, 10-Q) is cyclical.
+12% on FY28, fading toward mid-cycle growth. Used only for the one-month extension of NTM.

The fiscal year ends on the last Friday of August (10-Q). NTM from Oct-2027 = 11/12 FY28 + 1/12 FY29 = 3.52 + 0.36 = $3.88. Round 1 used CY2028 ($3.99), which reaches beyond the NTM window at the horizon and overstated value.

The 10-peer median on CY2027 is 18.95x (IQR 16.1-21.2x; the 8-core median is also 18.95x with JBL at 18.5x, or 18.4x with JBL at about 17x). I apply a 13% discount for persistent features, not sell-side calls: (1) 57% of sales is DRAM-price-driven Integrated Memory, which the market caps at about 6.6x at Micron; (2) top-10 customers are 66% of sales and one is 18.2% (FY25 10-K); (3) negative working-capital cash flow. This sits inside the peer range and applies the same discount as today's CY27 basis, without assuming that peer multiples change.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Corrected EV = 57.34M as-converted shares x $61.36 + $176M net debt = $3.69B. Proxy forward EBITDA $441M (TTM $173.9M / 0.395 GAAP-to-CY27 EPS scaler, the same proxy as the peers). Applying the 8.65x peer-median proxy gives EV $3.81B, less $176M net debt, / 57.34M = $63.4.

inputs_detail.value: $441M; PENG proxy multiple at today's price 8.4x vs peer median 8.65x
inputs_detail.derivation: For PENG and every peer alike: trailing EV/EBITDA x (TTM GAAP EPS / CY27 adjusted EPS); PENG's scaler is 0.395. It flatters names with large GAAP-to-non-GAAP gaps, so the weight is cut to 0.15.

Debt $750M 2031 + $140.0M 2030 (300 - 160 repurchased) + $14.5M 2029 (150 - 135.5) = $904.5M. Cash $440.3M + $735.1M net proceeds - $49.1M capped call - $136.7M - $161.4M repurchases - $100M term loan = $728.2M. Q4 cash flow is not yet known. At their fair values (10-Q: 260% / 143% of par) the 2029/2030 remainders would add about $84M of claims, or -$1.5/share.
The $200.5M preferred converts at $32.81 and is deep in the money, so I count it as shares (round 1 left it out entirely, which overstated this leg by about $9).

bear.story: DRAM/flash contract pricing peaks in 1H CY2027 and rolls over, and Integrated Memory (57% of sales) gives back much of its +111% growth. Non-hyperscale AI-factory wins stay lumpy and gross margin stays near 27%. FY27 EPS comes in at about $2.7-2.9 versus the $3.34 consensus and NTM EPS at the horizon is about $2.9, which at a 12x cyclical-trough multiple is about $35. A weak FY27 guide on Oct 6 or an interim-CFO miss would start this path.

base.story: FY27 delivers roughly the consensus $3.34 (about +28%), memory pricing normalises slowly into FY28, and FY28 EPS of about $3.84 makes NTM EPS at the horizon about $3.88. At 16.5x, a 13% discount to the 18.95x peer median for memory mix and concentration, that is about $64.

bull.story: AI memory (CXL, high-capacity modules) and the enterprise/neocloud/sovereign AI-factory business both compound, and SK hynix closes its purchase of the preferred as a strategic holder. FY27 beats toward $3.8 and NTM EPS at the horizon reaches about $4.6. The discount closes to about 21x, near the CLS/FN level: about $97-98, above the $89.86 52-week high.

comps_summary.peer_range: CY2027 P/E 6.6x (MU) to 26.4x (BHE), interquartile 16.1-21.2x; proxy forward EV/EBITDA 4.8x (MU) to 20.0x (FN). The basis is ONE calendar year, CY2027 street EPS: each fiscal-year Zacks consensus is month-weighted (Aug FYE 8/12 FY27 + 4/12 FY28; Jun 1/2 + 1/2; Sep 9/12 + 3/12; Oct 10/12 + 2/12; Mar 3/12 FY27 + 9/12 FY28; Jan: 1/12 FY Jan-27 + 11/12 FY Jan-28) and divided by the 2026-10-02 close. No stockanalysis 'Forward PE' is used. BHE uses stockanalysis CY27 EPS, which for a December FYE is already calendar-2027. The core-8 median (excluding MU and BHE) is 18.95x on my JBL figure and 18.4x on the supervisor's JBL of about 17x; my answer does not depend on which. PLXS (31.1x on Zacks CY27 $8.77) and NTAP (25.6x) were considered and left out: PLXS is defense/medical/industrial EMS with lower cyclicality, and NTAP is a storage-software mix. Including PLXS would raise the median to 19.4x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: PENG trades at 17.5x CY2027 EPS of $3.51, 8% under the 18.95x median. I apply 16.5x (13% under the median, inside the IQR) to NTM EPS at the horizon. The corrected EV proxy puts PENG at 8.4x versus the 8.65x median, roughly in line.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium. The 13% discount rests on features that persist through Oct-2027, not on sell-side calls. (1) Earnings mix: Integrated Memory was $275.1M of $478.7M Q3 sales, +111% y/y mostly on DRAM/flash price (Q3 8-K/10-Q), and the market capitalises peak memory earnings at about 6.6x (MU). That mix cannot change within 12 months. (2) Concentration: top-10 customers are 66% of FY25 sales, one Advanced Computing customer is 18.2% and one Integrated Memory customer 14.1% (FY25 10-K). (3) Cash conversion: operating cash flow turned negative on working capital in FY26 and the CFO post is interim. Offsetting this, PENG's ~28% non-GAAP gross margin is far above the EMS peers, so I stop well short of the bottom of the range (MU, SMCI).

thesis_break_reason: At $36 the stock would be about 10.3x CY2027 EPS of $3.51 and 9.3x my NTM-at-horizon base EPS. That is only consistent with FY27 tracking flat against FY26's ~$2.60 rather than the ~28% consensus growth: a memory-price reversal hitting Integrated Memory, loss or deferral of key AI-infrastructure customers, or a guidance cut, not ordinary volatility. It also sits about where my bear-case NTM EPS of about $2.9 meets a trough 12x multiple.

reasoning: Round 2 starts from my round-1 primary-document work and takes on the supervisor's verified corrections, two of which I re-checked first-hand on EDGAR. The July 17 8-K confirms $750M of 0% 2031 notes, $735.1M net proceeds, a $49.1M capped call, $135.5M of 2029 and $160.0M of 2030 notes repurchased, and the $100M term loan repaid. That leaves $14.5M of 2029 and $140M of 2030 notes and puts principal net debt at about $176M, not my round-1 $68M. The July 28 13D/A confirms SK Telecom's sale of all 200,000 preferred (6,096,104 as-converted shares, 10.3%) to an SK hynix subsidiary for $380.3M, pending regulatory approval, so I replaced my 'preferred-holder selling overhang' catalyst with a positive one. EDGAR shows no 8-K since July. I fixed 9M EPS ($1.83, so Q4 is implied at $0.77, in line with the street) and dropped my unsupported 5-10% government-share estimate in favour of about 0.2% visible and 1-3% all-in. Valuation: I made two changes of my own beyond the supervisor's. (a) The main P/E method now uses NTM EPS at the horizon ($3.88, about FY28) instead of CY2028, which reached beyond the window the market will price in Oct-2027. (b) The EV leg now counts the preferred as 6.10M shares and uses principal net debt, which takes it from $72.8 to $63.4. The peer set stays at 10 on one CY2027 Zacks basis, with a median of 18.95x (DELL corrected to 19.4x). I keep a 13% discount (16.5x), argued from persistent mix, concentration and cash-conversion features, so fair value is about $64. I disagree mildly with the supervisor's $61, which applies 16x to FY28 with no roll to NTM. My scenarios are $35 / $64 / $98 at 27 / 50 / 23%, which gives a probability-weighted mean of $64.0 that reconciles exactly with fair value. I built the ladder as a mixture of lognormals (sigmas 0.33 / 0.22 / 0.27, each with mean equal to its scenario price), so the median is about $61 (right skew) and the effective vol is about 60%, below the 83% realised, which is inflated by the +127% re-rating. I fattened the extreme tails slightly for event risk. The 1-month ladder is near-symmetric around $61.4 because the Oct 6 print has no clear edge. Research limits: I used about 5 of the 8 extra lookups. sec.gov direct fetch failed, so the filings were read through WebFetch. The USAspending figures are the supervisor's rerun, which I did not repeat.
